observed.text: t t t t t t t t
observed.note: the collapse is present at the FIRST decode token, not at step four. The earlier 'three good tokens then repeats' reading came from a run whose first tokens happened to be plausible; with this prompt the very first emitted token is already wrong.

eliminated.hypothesis: position, KV slot or sequence length stops advancing
eliminated.method: HAWKING_DS_TRACE prints pos, seq_slot and seq_len after every forward
eliminated.result: all three advance monotonically for every token, prefill and decode alike

eliminated.hypothesis: MoE routing is frozen (every token takes the same experts)
eliminated.method: read moe_route_ids_buf after each committed command buffer
eliminated.result: routes vary per token: [56,9,57,14,10,34] at pos 0 through [57,11,29,50,59,14] at pos 11
eliminated.self_correction: an earlier read of route_history_buf returned all zeros and I nearly recorded frozen routing. That buffer is only written when expert_cache is Some, so the zeros were a probe artifact. moe_route_ids_buf is written by every MoE layer unconditionally and is the correct place to look.

eliminated.hypothesis: the autotuned Q4_K GEMM schedule is wrong for this layout
eliminated.method: replaced gemm_q4_k_schedule per_shape/v3_dual with scalar and reran
eliminated.result: byte-identical output. The schedule is not the cause.

eliminated.hypothesis: the routed-expert path alone is at fault
eliminated.method: --speculate exact-shared, whose draft is a shared-expert-only forward
eliminated.result: accept 0/14. Shared-only and full disagree on every token and both are degenerate, so the defect is not confined to the routed path.

incidental_findings.finding: prefill runs one token per forward through the decode path
incidental_findings.evidence: one trace line per prompt token
incidental_findings.consequence: 91.7 ms per prompt token against llama.cpp's 0.76 on the same file. This family has no batched prefill at all, which is a larger gap than the 14B's batch-8 ceiling and a different one.

incidental_findings.finding: the last prompt token is fed twice
incidental_findings.evidence: in=317 at pos=5 (prefill) and again at pos=6 (first decode)
incidental_findings.assessment: NOT the defect. qwen_dense uses the same convention (prefill over every prompt token, then decode seeded with prompt_ids.last() at pos=prompt_len) and answers 'The capital of France is' with ' Paris'. It costs one extra forward and one duplicate KV entry per request; it does not collapse the output.
incidental_findings.left_alone: changing it would move a working adapter's output for no measured gain

why_this_stops_here: the next step is a numerics bisect, and there is nothing to bisect against. deepseek_v2 has no CPU forward: mla_decode hard-errors with 'Metal context unavailable on this platform', so there is no second implementation of MLA in the tree to diff layer by layer. The legacy non-Wedge-C path that could have served as one was retired, and the message that says so dates to the dismantle->hawking rename. Building a numpy or CPU reference for Q4_K dequant plus MLA plus MoE is the missing instrument, and it is a piece of work in its own right rather than a continuation of this bisect.
consequence_for_the_mission: the admitted MoE proof is NOT obtained. DeepSeek-V2-Lite is admitted as far as loading, routing and decoding at 35.98 tok/s, and it is wrong. A speed number from a model that emits garbage does not establish a grammar win, so no MoE kernel is promoted on its evidence.
